1
What is the approximate average speed of a winning female Olympic athlete running a 100 m
race?
A
6 m s–1
B
9 m s–1
C
12 m s–1
D
15 m s–1

hints: Start from the definition of average speed for the $100 \text{ m}$ race: average speed equals total distance divided by total time.
Recall a sensible winning time for a female Olympic $100 \text{ m}$ final, which is a little over $10 \text{ s}$, around $10.5 \text{ s}$ to $11 \text{ s}$.
Divide $100 \text{ m}$ by your estimated time in seconds and see which listed speed in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ it is closest to.
walkthrough: Identify the given distance: $s = 100 \text{ m}$ for the $100 \text{ m}$ race.
State the rule for average speed: $v = s/t$, where $t$ is the total race time.
Estimate the winning time: an elite female Olympic champion runs about $10.5 \text{ s}$ to $11 \text{ s}$.
Substitute values with units: $v \approx 100 \text{ m} / 11 \text{ s} \approx 9.1 \text{m s}^{-1}$.
Check reasonableness: this is much faster than jogging but well below impossible times under $9 \text{ s}$, and the unit is $\text{m s}^{-1}$ as required.
Match $\approx 9 \text{m s}^{-1}$ to the options. This is option B.

A.explanation: A speed of $6 \text{m s}^{-1}$ would need a time of about $17 \text{ s}$ for $100 \text{ m}$, which is far too slow for an Olympic winner.

B.explanation: A winning time of about $11 \text{ s}$ gives $100/11 \approx 9 \text{m s}^{-1}$, which matches elite female sprinting.

C.explanation: A speed of $12 \text{m s}^{-1}$ would need a time of about $8.3 \text{ s}$, which is faster than the women's world record.

D.explanation: A speed of $15 \text{m s}^{-1}$ would need a time of about $6.7 \text{ s}$, which is impossible for a human over $100 \text{ m}$.
